name: DFRobot DFR0534 voice module
//: A UART-controlled audio module with its own flash and an onboard amplifier.

needs.note: The host TRANSMITS into the module's receive pin. The module's own TXD is deliberately left unwired: nothing reads its replies, and its idle level is not something a 3.3 V pin should be asked to tolerate.

power.note: bridged amplifier output — never ground either side
power.//direction: An OUTPUT, not a supply. Both halves of a bridged amplifier: they swing in opposite directions and the speaker sits across them. Wiring them to one net shorts the amplifier to itself.
An OUTPUT, not a supply. Both halves of a bridged amplifier: they swing in opposite directions and the speaker sits across them. Wiring them to one net shorts the amplifier to itself.

has_enable_pin.source: the module's header carries no enable
has_enable_pin.why_it_matters: It cannot be told to sleep. On a battery design the only way to stop it drawing is to cut its rail, which is a decision the BOARD has to make before it is fabricated.

idle_current_ma.source: third-party measurement of a JQ8400 board, the same decoder this module uses (github.com/arduino12/mp3_player_module_wire): 18 mA idle, 4.5 mA after the one-wire sleep command, and 140 uA only after removing the BUSY LED and cutting the amplifier's SD pin to a GPIO. DFRobot publish no figure for the DFR0534 itself and no schematic, so its floor cannot be known from documentation
idle_current_ma.why_it_matters: Even the optimistic 4.5 mA is roughly ten times the entire rest of a sleeping battery board. With no standby command and no schematic, the module's power has to be switched in hardware — which is a board decision, not a firmware one.

mounting_holes.value: 2 holes, 15.00 mm apart, both 3.50 mm in from the right edge
mounting_holes.source: DFRobot's own dimension drawing, https://dfimg.dfrobot.com/wiki/19342/DFR0534_mp3-player-module_dimension_V1.0.pdf (agrees with the datasheet p.1 and the wiki)
mounting_holes.note: Drill measures ~2.5 mm off the drawing, which is M2 clearance — NOT M3. DFRobot does not label the diameter, so treat the size as unconfirmed even though the spacing is dimensioned.

has_uart_standby_command.source: DFRobot's 11-page datasheet and the JQ8400 manual both document opcodes 0x01-0x26 and neither includes sleep or standby; the JQ8400 manual says sleep is entered over a one-wire protocol it then describes as untested
has_uart_standby_command.note: Settles an open question: there is no software way to put this module to sleep, so cutting its power in hardware is the only option.

host_requirements: Give it a reservoir capacitor at its supply pin. A speaker peak pulls hundreds of milliamps and the resulting sag is a classic brownout reset.

If the design sleeps, put a high-side switch on its rail and hold the gate OFF with a resistor — the host's GPIO goes high-impedance during deep sleep and reset, which is exactly when the module must be off.
It boots from cold whenever its rail returns, so nothing may be sent for a few hundred milliseconds after power-up.

body_mm.source: DFRobot's own dimension drawing, https://dfimg.dfrobot.com/wiki/19342/DFR0534_mp3-player-module_dimension_V1.0.pdf (agrees with the datasheet p.1 and the wiki)
body_mm.note: Thickness and component height are NOT published by DFRobot. The tallest features are the two side-entry JST-PH sockets and the micro-USB; measure them before designing an enclosure.
